name: d90_25m
rationale: THE THRESHOLD IS NOT SETTLED -- the roll-rate analysis reported no point of no return and this is its fallback. Threshold set by the roll-rate analysis across the halves of the performance window: INCONCLUSIVE -- no rung reached 75% deterioration among its movers, so on this book every measured rung still cures more often than it rolls across the window. Quoted is the deepest readable rung (90+ DPD, 54.7%), which is a floor on the threshold rather than a recommendation. A book observed over a benign window will do this. Read across the two halves of the 53-month window (26 months observed, 27 predicted): the worst rung a loan reached in the first half against the worst it reached in the second. Every window length looked at picks the same rungTHE WINDOW IS A DELIBERATE OVERRIDE, SHORTER than the 75% capture the vintage recommends (53 months): 50% capture was asked for instead. Roughly 50% of a cohort's bads arrive after month 25 and will be labelled GOOD. The 25-month window is the age by which 50% of a cohort's OWN bads have arrived, as the median over the 98 cohorts at least that deep -- a self-consistent fixed point, not a share of a pooled total (horizon 122 months). It is the median over the 98 cohorts at least that deep, of 120 in the panel, and the middle half of them put it between 23 and 31 months. By that age 53.6% of the bads those cohorts eventually show have arrived.
description: An observation is bad if the loan reaches the threshold in any month of the window, where the threshold is 90-119 days past due (25-month performance window).  A terminal credit-event disposition (third party sale, short sale or charge off, REO disposition) inside the window also counts as bad. A special-mention event (a modification, a payment deferral, a forbearance or repayment plan, or principal made non-interest-bearing) also counts as bad, because a workout resets the delinquency clock and would otherwise be recorded as a cure. Accommodation attributed to a declared disaster is excluded.
